clue.text: One protecting fence offering nothing, so arrested in Greek island

indicators.note: being arrested in the island means being held inside its name

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
nothing is zero, the round letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guarding a fence turns up empty-handed and is detained on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One protecting fence' reads like a guard, but it is the tarry wood preservative; 'arrested in' signals the holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is the tarry oil painted on wooden fences to preserve them from rot.

clue.text: A nod and a few winks

explanation.definitionFit: A short sleep is called a nod or forty winks.

clue.text: Puzzling variations?

clue.text: Makes casserole, as tea spoils

explanation.surface: Someone cooks a casserole while the pot of tea goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook slowly in liquid is to braise, and tea left too long brewing turns bitter in the same way.

explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or stay, so tarried means lingered.

explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted over and over during meditation.

clue.text: Taking in charge for striking

explanation.definitionFit: A toiletry is any article such as soap or shampoo for washing and grooming.

clue.text: Quick to give reminder

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be fast in jogging another person's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means immediate or punctual, and as a verb means to cue someone with words they have forgotten.

clue.text: Woman's love for great man

explanation.walkthrough: Love means nil in tennis scoring, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a celebrated figure admired for courage or achievement.

clue.text: A corps devastated cities, bringing end to war

explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for the Royal Marines, a British military corps; 'devastated' signals the anagram of the last word.

clue.text: With fly about, left the chamber

explanation.surface: Someone with a fly buzzing round them walks out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SOAR around L. The definition is an old word: a solar was the private upper room of a medieval house.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval houses the solar was the family's private upstairs room.

clue.text: Ran exercise in borders of Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, so it is a synonym for moved fast.

clue.text: Don't give up power Irish always held

explanation.walkthrough: ERSE is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland; 'held' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is to carry on rather than quit.

clue.text: Antarctic explorer accepted constant numbers

pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: A polar explorer took on board a fixed set of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' is read as things that numb, not figures; 'accepted' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are drugs that deaden pain, so they are things that make a person numb.

clue.text: Working model is hard to destroy

explanation.definitionFit: To raze or pull down a building is to wreck it completely.

clue.text: Start to draw on one particular line of capital

explanation.definitionFit: The District line is one of the routes of the London Underground.

clue.text: Pithy expression covering English farm animals

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
a ram is a male sheep, another farm animal

explanation.surface: A short witty saying about English livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase, 'farm animals', supplies two animals in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying, a concise and clever remark.

clue.text: Mark a card — a club

an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Someone marks an ace in the club suit of a pack of cards.

clue.text: Ancient clothing made from goat

clue.text: Reptile moving around in shade
